content.title: Eye Drops Are Being Recalled Nationwide—Over 3 Million Bottles Affected
content.text: Check your eye drops ASAP. Published on April 3, 2026 Credit: Design elements: Getty Images. EatingWell design. Over 3 million bottles of eye drops are recalled due to sterility concerns, per the FDA.Affected brands include Walgreens, CVS, Kroger, Rite Aid and more.Stop using recalled products and contact the retailer to confirm lot codes for a refund. There’s a recall on approximately 3,111,072 bottles of eye drops sold nationwide, according to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA). This is due to “lack of assurance of sterility.” The following products, alongside the affected brands, have been recalled. If you have any of these eye drop bottles on hand, stop using them and contact your place of purchase to confirm recalled lot codes and expiration dates to request a refund. Sterile Eye Drops AC (tetrahydrozoline HCl 0.05%, zinc sulfate 0.25%) in 0.5 fl. oz. (15 mL) bottles sold under the following brand names are affected: Best ChoiceGood Neighbor PharmacyGood SenseKrogerLeaderP by PublixQuality ChoiceTopCare For questions about this recall, contact the FDA at 1-888-INFO-FDA (1-888-463-6332). This was recently classified as a Class II recall, meaning that the eye drops “may cause temporary or medically reversible adverse health consequences.” If you are experiencing any health concerns after using the recalled eye drops, contact a healthcare provider immediately.
